Google Health and Strava

The Google Health and Strava integration has been updated. You can now automatically sync any activity you log in Google Health to Strava.

​

Comparing the updated integration to the previous one

  • More activity types: You can sync any activity type logged in Google Health to Strava, with or without GPS. The previous integration only supported bikes, runs, hikes, and walks recorded with GPS.
  • More control: You can now choose which activity types sync to Strava.

How to update your connection

To take advantage of the updates, update your connection using one of the options below. If you don’t update your connection, only bikes, runs, hikes, and walks with GPS will continue to sync.

  • Starting in the Strava app: Go to You > Settings > Connect an app or device > Google Health.
  • Starting in the Google Health app: Go to your account settings (top right) > Partner Apps > Strava (listed under Add connections).

Choosing which activities sync

You can control which activities sync to Strava from the Google Health app. Go to account settings (top right) > Partner Apps > Strava > Activity writing, then select the activity types you want synced.

Once connected, new activities sync automatically from Google Health to Strava. To export a previous activity from Google Health and upload it directly to Strava, refer to Google Health’s data export instructions. Note: Any changes you make to an activity in the Google Health app will not be reflected in Strava.

Important: Activities logged in Strava will no longer sync to Google Health via the Strava integration, regardless of your connection settings. We’re working with Google to enable more options for logging activities from Strava to Google Health.

​

Google Health data isn’t syncing to Strava

Work through these steps:

  • Reconnect your accounts and confirm you’ve accepted the option to “Upload your activities from Google Health to Strava.” Then sync your Fitbit tracker or Pixel Watch and wait an hour.

  • Confirm you aren’t recording the same exercise in the Strava app and Google Health app at the same time.

  • Confirm you recorded a new exercise after connecting your accounts. Activities recorded before connecting won’t be uploaded. If those steps don’t work, export the activity as a TCX file from Google Health and upload it to Strava:

  • In the Google Health app, tap the Fitness tab.

  • Select the activity you want to export.

  • Tap the three dots, then tap Export.

  • Share or save the file to your device, then upload it to Strava.

How to Fix GPS Recording Issues on Huawei Phones

Usually, battery-saving settings on Huawei phones are the cause of most GPS troubles. These settings can force quit the GPS at any time, which means that the Strava app cannot continue to record your activity. Try these tips when recording with a Huawei phone:

  • Check that you’re running the latest updates of both the Strava app and your Android device.

  • Next, be sure to add Strava as a ‘protected app’ in your phone’s settings and disable or ignore any energy optimizations or battery-saving modes.

  • An option shared by our community is to prevent the auto-lock of the Strava record screen. Leaving the screen on for the duration of the recording may prevent the phone from shutting the GPS off. A list of some Huawei devices with recording issues:

  • Android 6 devices

    • Huawei Nova, Nova +
    • Huawei P8, P8 Lite
    • Huawei G7, G7 Plus
    • Huawei Mate 7, Mate S
    • Huawei Honor 7, 6, 6 Plus
    • Honor 7, 6, 6 Plus, 4C

  • Android 7 devices

    • Huawei Mate 9, 8
    • Huawei P9, P9 Plus, P9 Lite
    • Honor 8

How to Use Auto-Pause on iOS

When Auto-Pause is enabled, the Strava iOS app will automatically pause when you are resting during your activity. Auto-pause alleviates the need to manually pause your activity each time you stop.

Enabling Auto-Pause

  • Select Record from the bottom navigation menu.
  • Expand the menu by sliding it up from the bottom of your screen, and select Auto-Pause on the next page.
  • Toggle auto-pause ON and OFF for runs only, rides only, both runs and rides, or neither.

How Auto-Pause Works

Auto-Pause ON

​

​Auto-pause for cycling uses GPS movement to automatically detect when you are at rest. It’s important to note that the app will only pause when you’re completely stopped. Once you begin moving again, Auto-pause will turn off. Because this feature is GPS-based, it’s important to note that if you are taking a break to go indoors or someplace where the GPS line of sight is obscured, you should use the manual pause feature to prevent any miscalculations. Cycling auto-pause will be on by default but can be turned off on your settings page.

​

Auto-[ause for running is motion-based and uses your accelerometer to automatically detect when you are at rest. Athletes will hear audio announcements for auto-pause events if they have split announcements on or Live Segment audio enabled.

Auto-Pause OFF

​

If you choose to turn auto-pause off, Strava will calculate your moving and resting time during the upload process instead of during the activity.

​

For Runs with auto-pause disabled, we will do server-side resting time calculations (per above) unless there are manual pause events. If there are manual pause events, we assume that you want to control the time and will calculate moving time with respect to timer time instead.

Have problems with Auto-Pause?

Typically, problems with auto-pause are actually caused by problems with your GPS or other location services. The simplest fix is to turn your phone off, then back on again, and flip your GPS or location services off and then back on. You may also want to review our Troubleshooting GPS Issues and try those fixes as well. If you continue to have problems, please proceed with submitting a support ticket.

​

​Keep in mind that if you manually pause the app, you must manually resume the app before continuing your activity, even if you have auto-pause enabled.

​

​To share your feedback and discuss troubleshooting tips, please see this article.

iFIT and Strava

Connecting your iFIT account to Strava

Once the connection has been established, all of your iFIT activities from any iFIT-enabled equipment that is signed in to your account will sync to Strava whenever you open the iFIT app on your smartphone.

  • Open the iFIT app on your mobile device.

  • From the iFIT app, navigate to the Settings menu and select Connected Apps > Strava > Connect.

  • You will be prompted to log in with your Strava credentials.

  • After logging in, select Authorize.

  • Your iFIT and Strava accounts are now connected. All of your activities will now be synchronized between iFIT and Strava.

  • Select Done. Activities recorded in Strava will sync to iFIT, and activities performed in iFIT will also be synced to Strava, keeping all of your workout histories up to date on both platforms. Please note that Strava activities synced to iFIT will be private and only visible to the account member who owns the activity.

  • If you want to customize your activity, including import and export settings between iFIT and Strava, you can adjust the Permissions toggle on and off.

  • To post workout activities to Strava, ensure the toggle is switched on. To stop posting workout activities, switch the toggle off.

  • To import workout activities from Strava, ensure the toggle is switched on. To stop importing workout activities, switch the toggle off.

Disconnecting your iFIT and Strava Accounts

  • From the iFIT app, navigate to the Settings menu and select Connected Apps > Strava > Disconnect.
  • When a system pop-up box appears asking you to confirm your selection, select Remove.
  • Your iFIT and Strava accounts are now disconnected. Your activities will no longer be synchronized between iFIT and Strava.

FAQs

Will my past activities be synced after connecting my accounts?

At this time, only activities that are recorded after your accounts are connected will be synced between accounts.

If I delete an activity in Strava, will it also delete the activity in iFIT?

Yes, deleting an activity in Strava will delete the activity in iFIT if the activity was initially created in Strava. However, deleting an activity in iFIT will not delete it from Strava.

Why aren’t my Strava or iFIT activities syncing?

To begin, make sure you have an active internet connection, then refresh the iFIT and Strava applications. If the activity still does not sync, wait a few hours and then refresh the applications again. If problems syncing your activities still persist, you may have to reauthorize the connection between iFIT and Strava. To do this, start by fully disconnecting your accounts. Then, reconnect your accounts by following the instructions under “Connecting your iFIT account to Strava.”

Why are some of my workout metrics, like calories and distance, displayed differently between iFIT and Strava?

Due to the way iFIT and Strava calculate and interpret an activity’s data, certain workout metrics may display differently, even when based on the same activity.

Recording Activities on Ladder:

  • You will then be prompted to start an activity in the Ladder app from your iPhone.
    • Opening the Ladder app first will also work if your Apple Watch is connected to your iPhone.
    • The app will display a prompt if your watch is connected and ready for the workout.
  • Select your workout after approving health permissions.
  • You can then control the workout and view your heart rate on your Apple Watch while the activity is in progress on your iPhone.
  • After connecting to Strava, any completed activities will automatically sync from Ladder.

Live Segments on Strava Apple Watch app

Live Segments brings the experience of competing on a ride or run segment directly to your Apple Watch. All Strava athletes receive real-time updates and haptic cues when entering a segment, keeping you motivated and engaged. Strava subscribers unlock additional advanced features.

Selecting Segments

Live Segments are a feature available for outdoor running and riding activities. There are two types of segments, popular and starred. Your location determines popular segments, while starred segments are those you’ve personally selected.

To “Star” a segment, tap the star icon next to its name. If you do this before your ride, the starred segment will be active during your activity. The Strava app does not prioritize starred segments over popular ones in the live experience; the closest segment, whether starred or popular, will enter live mode.

Please note that downhill segments are not synced to devices for Strava Live Segments. Our system recognizes even the slightest negative grade, so some segments displaying a 0% grade may still be considered downhill and will not sync to your device.

Competing in a Segment

You can switch back to the stats page during your Live Segment attempt by swiping up on the screen, and view the Live Segment progress in the top left corner.

When you are approaching a Starred Segment, your watch will vibrate and automatically display the Live Segment view. For popular segments, your watch will not vibrate or automatically transition; you can access the Live Segment view from the stats page by clicking the horseshoe icon.

As you approach the segment’s start, your watch will show the “Go!” state. Once you begin the segment, you will see your progress in real-time. You can return to the stats page during a Live Segment attempt by swiping up, and monitor your progress in the top left corner.

FAQs

Can I turn Live Segments off?

Yes. Live Segment alerts are enabled by default. To disable them, open the Strava Apple Watch app, swipe left, tap Settings, scroll down, and toggle off Live Segments.

As a Strava Subscriber, what advanced capabilities will I see?

Strava subscribers receive several enhanced features for segments:

  • Live Segment Comparison: See your current time against your personal record in real-time.
  • Distance Countdown: Track the remaining distance in a segment.
  • Time/Countdown Toggle: Easily switch between viewing your time and the countdown by tapping.
  • Post-Segment Results: Compare your performance against your personal record immediately upon completing a segment.
Can I use Live Segments as a free athlete?

Yes, free athletes can use Live Segments. They will be able to see if they are ahead or behind their personal record (PR) time, indicated by an arrow and a green or red color, but the exact time difference will not be displayed.

What if I don’t have a personal record (PR) on a segment?

Subscribers on their first attempt will only see the distance countdown statistic.

Why is my segment time different on Apple Watch than after upload?

Preliminary times displayed on the watch app may differ from final times calculated after uploading to Strava. This is due to the watch app and Strava’s leaderboard system using different algorithms to detect start and finish points. The final calculation ensures fairness and consistency for all athletes.

Connecting Strava and lululemon Studio Mirror

Syncing From lululemon Studio to Strava

FAQs

Why is my activity not appearing on Strava/not exporting from Strava into lululemon Studio?

You can try the following steps to troubleshoot the issue:

  • Confirm your lululemon studio mirror and app are on the latest software versions:
    • See here for instructions to update.
    • Leave the mirror powered on and in sleep mode overnight to receive background updates. See here for more info about putting your mirror to sleep.
    • The next morning, turn your mirror off and on using the switch on the bottom.
  • Check your Settings:
    • Use the toggles for Auto upload to Strava or Auto import from Strava (under the Settings tab) as needed.
    • Toggle your preferred selection off and back on.
  • Uninstall & reinstall the lululemon Studio and/or Strava Apps:
    • Uninstall and reinstall the app from your phone/tablet.
    • If the issue persists, please also uninstall and reinstall the Strava app.

Meta Glasses and Strava

Strava athletes can now overlay their performance metrics directly onto their photos and videos captured with Oakley and Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. This integration lets you create dynamic, shareable moments that show off both your effort and your perspective on the move.

Media captured during your activity can be shared to the Strava activity recorded at that same time, allowing your photos and videos to pair with your workout automatically. You can also share your media on Instagram, Facebook, and other social media platforms.

Connecting Strava to Meta Glasses

To connect your Strava account, open the Meta AI app and navigate to the Glasses tab. From there, select Settings (the gear icon), then choose App Connections → Strava → Connect Strava. You’ll be prompted to log in and authorize the connection.

If you’d like to disconnect your accounts, return to the same menu and select Disconnect Strava.

Overlaying Your Performance Metrics

To add Strava stats to your photos or videos, open your Meta AI Gallery and select the media you want to edit. Tap Stats, choose the metrics you’d like to display—such as distance, pace, heart rate, or power—then tap Save. When you share to Strava, the edited media will automatically sync with the activity you recorded during that time.

FAQs

Does this integration work with all Meta glasses?

No. The integration is compatible with all Oakley Meta and Ray-Ban Meta glasses, except for Ray-Ban Stories, which are not supported.

What accounts do I need?

You’ll need the Meta AI app, which can be created with an email address or linked to an existing Facebook or Instagram account.

Can I share media to any Strava activity?

Media can only be shared with the Strava activity that took place during the same time frame as your recording. However, you can export your media to your phone’s Photos app and manually upload it to a different activity if you prefer.

What types of metrics can I overlay?

You can overlay both summary and real-time metrics, including distance, pace, heart rate, and power.

Connecting Strava and the Mi Fitness App

You can download the Mi Fitness app (formerly known as Xiaomi Wear) to pair and connect your Xiaomi watch to Strava.

iOS

  • Log in to the Mi Fitness app.
  • Open Profile > Connected Apps.
  • Tap the button next to Strava to authorize Mi Fitness to connect to Strava.
  • Tap Authorize and log in to your Strava account to complete.

Android

  • Select the Profile tab in the lower right corner of the app.
  • Tap on Settings and then select Third Party Data.
  • If you have the Strava mobile application installed, you should see it listed under Accounts and Authorization.
  • Select Strava from the list of apps, this will prompt you to log in to your Strava profile for verification and connection.
  • Select the permissions you would like Mi Fitness to access on Strava, then select Authorize.

Troubleshooting Syncing

There are a few reasons why your Mi Fitness activities may not be syncing to Strava.

Your device may not be connected to the phone via Bluetooth.

  • To check if your device is connected to the phone via Bluetooth, for Android, go to Settings > Connections > Bluetooth and look for your device. For iOS, go to Settings > Bluetooth and look for your device under My Devices. Your device may have been disconnected from Strava.

  • To check permissions, on your phone, go to Settings > Applications. Check the permissions section of each app, Strava, and Mi Fitness, to ensure all permissions have been granted. Bad or corrupted data coverage areas can cause sync issues.

  • Check your data coverage area; both Strava and Mi Fitness need an active internet connection to load, refresh, or sync data between them. If syncing fails, check that you are in a good data coverage area.

  • Make sure you have a strong signal before starting an activity and that your device is up to date with the latest firmware. Lastly, check that your Mi Fitness app is updated. If, after recording a new activity, you are still noticing the same issue, please reach out to Mi Fitness support for additional troubleshooting steps. You can find support for your location here.

FAQs

My activity does not have GPS, can I still sync it from Mi Fitness to Strava?

Mi Fitness activities that do not contain GPS data can sync to Strava, but they will not include the distance data we need to process this information. Without it, we are unable to add distance to these activities. You can continue to sync your Mi Fitness activities to Strava as they are currently syncing, or you can choose to create manual activities using the data available in the Mi Fitness app. You can learn more about creating a manual activity here.

Moving time too short and pace too fast on Suunto activities?

This may be the result of how the GPS points are recorded in the activity file. If the file contains data points with time, but without GPS updates, when we parse the data, it looks like you’re not moving at those points. This causes problems in how we calculate resting time, which results in inaccuracies in pace calculations and moving time. We are working with Suunto to resolve the issue, but in the meantime, here are some workarounds that may give you a more realistic analysis:

  • Swap your distance stream to remove any outlier points from the device recording and rely on the GPS data instead.
    • Click on the link directly below your current distance listed on the activity details page, where it says Distance(?) in small letters.
    • From the pop-up, click Correct Distance.
    • When the status changes from “Calculating” to “Updated,” refresh the page.
    • If you would like to revert the change, you can click the same link and click Revert Distance.
  • Tag the activity as a race to force the activity to read the total elapsed time instead of the moving time.
    • Go to the edit screen for the activity in question.
    • Select Race under the Run Type drop-down menu.
    • Save your changes.

Nike and Strava

Strava athletes can automatically sync their activities from the Nike Run Club (NRC) and Nike Training Club (NTC) apps to their ​​Strava accounts.

Connecting Nike to Strava

Setting up the connection with Strava on either the Nike Run Club or Training Club app will enable syncing for both apps.

  • Open the Nike Run Club or Nike Training Club app.
  • Tap your profile initials in the upper left-hand of the screen.
  • Select Settings > Partners.
  • Select Strava on the Partners page.
  • Complete the setup in the connect screen that pops up.
  • If the apps are successfully connected, you will see the Strava and Nike icons on a screen with a green check mark.

How It Works

Once you’ve successfully connected your accounts, both the Nike Run Club and Nike Training Club apps will automatically sync newly recorded activities.

Nike Run Club will allow you to sync your indoor and outdoor run activities. If you have paired a heart rate sensor to your NRC app or are using an Apple Watch, you will be able to record your heart rate on your Nike activity, which will be displayed on Strava. Calories will only be calculated when heart rate is recorded on an activity.

Nike Training Club will sync workouts with a short video snippet from the workout that you completed. Yoga, HIIT, and weight training activities will sync over as the corresponding sport type on Strava and all other Nike workouts will be listed as a Workout.

Disconnecting Nike From Strava

From the Strava website:

  • Log into your account on the Strava website.
  • Hover over your profile picture in the upper right corner and select Settings from the dropdown menu.
  • Open My Apps from the menu on the left-hand side.
  • Click on the Revoke Access button next to the Nike app to automatically disconnect your account from Nike. From the Nike Run Club app:

The option to disconnect your Nike account from other apps is only available in the Nike Run Club app, but activities from both the NRC and NTC will stop syncing to Strava once the accounts are disconnected.

  • Open Settings > Partners.
  • Tap the link at the bottom of the partners’ page to view your account on Nike.com.
  • Tap disconnect next to Strava to disconnect it from your Nike accounts.

FAQs

Can I sync my previously recorded activities from Nike Run Club and Nike Training Club?

At this time, only activities recorded after connecting your accounts will sync to Strava. There is no way to sync or import your historic activities.

If I edit my activity on NRC, will it update my activity on Strava?

Any edits made on NRC after your activity has been synced will not be reflected on Strava, as those edits do not actually change the activity file that has already been synced to Strava.

Will my activities on Strava sync to Nike?

Currently, the integration will only push your activities from Nike apps to Strava and cannot pull activity data recorded from other devices/apps from Strava.

I completed a Nike-sponsored Strava Challenge but did not get my prize.

You can read more about how sponsored Strava Challenges work here: Strava Challenges

No Movement Detected on Apple Watch

If you’re receiving a message on your Apple Watch app that says “No Movement Detected,” it could be that the Watch isn’t getting a proper GPS signal while activity is being recorded. When the activity has finished without GPS data, the app will mistakenly think that no movement was detected. We rely on GPS data to process your activity. Without this information, an activity can have issues syncing to our server. You may still see data during your activity that is coming from the Watch’s pedometer. Apple’s Activity app uses the watch’s accelerometer to record data, so this will function even if GPS hasn’t been acquired. To prevent this in the future,

  • Wait until you’re outdoors to open the Strava Watch app and wait for about a minute until you start an activity. This will allow the Watch to collect a stronger GPS signal, which will prevent these discrepancies from occurring.
  • Try uninstalling/reinstalling the Strava app on both your iPhone and Apple Watch.
    • Use the Watch app located on your iPhone to force an uninstall of the Strava Watch app. Note that it may take some time for the app to be fully uninstalled from the Watch face.
    • Confirm the app has been uninstalled from the Watch.
    • Uninstall the Strava app from your iPhone.
    • Force close all apps on the iPhone.
    • Restart the Watch and iPhone.
    • Download and install the Strava app on the iPhone.
    • Confirm you are logged into the Strava app.
    • Confirm the Strava app has been installed on the Apple Watch.
    • Unlock the display on the iPhone and load the Strava Apple Watch app.
    • Watch for and approve prompts on both devices.

Oura and Strava

Connect the Oura app to Strava to share recorded media to any Strava activities that are already synced to your account. This will allow you to add additional information and media to your existing Strava activities, even those not recorded with Oura. See a more holistic view of all the efforts and activities you complete in your training.

Connecting Strava and Oura

  • From the Oura app, tap the icon in the upper left corner of the home screen.
  • Tap Settings.
  • Tap App Integrations in the Data sharing section.
  • Tap the Strava option and review details of what benefits the Strava integration will provide, and then tap Continue.
  • Authorize permission for Strava to access the user’s specified Oura data. You must enter your Strava login credentials to grant this access.
  • Receive confirmation that the integration was successful and configure the integration to either import only, export only, or import and export. By default, import and export will both be toggled ON.

Syncing From Strava to Oura

Once your accounts are connected and you’ve enabled imports, Strava activities will be automatically displayed as activity cards within the Oura app. Strava activities will count towards your activity goal and Activity Score in the Oura App.

Syncing From Oura to Strava

Once your accounts are connected and you’ve enabled imports, activities captured using the Workout Heart Rate (WHR) recording feature will automatically sync to Strava. Please be aware that manual and auto-detected activities recorded by Oura cannot be synced to Strava at this time.

Sharing Media on Activities

Connect the Oura app to Strava to share media using Oura’s Stickers to illustrate your unique health story. This will allow you to add additional information via the data insights added to the images and media to your existing Strava activities. See a more holistic view of all the efforts and activities you complete in your training

Connecting to Strava :

  • Create or log in to your Oura account

  • Click on the three-bar icon in the top left and go to ‘Settings’

  • In Settings, go to the section labeled Data Sharing and select ‘Other Apps’

  • You will then see the option to Connect with Strava, and you can toggle on or off the ability to sync Oura activities to Strava or pull Strava activities into Oura. Sharing Readiness Scores and other media from Oura to Strava:

  • Once Oura is connected to Strava, go to the main ‘Today’ screen view

  • Click the share icon in the top right

  • From here, you can choose which metrics to display and the background image

  • Select ‘Share to Strava’

  • A list of your most recent activities in Strava will populate and you can select which one to share your Oura data to.

FAQ

Why is my activity missing an image?

Be sure that you’ve enabled the Oura partner integration from this page on the Strava website or under Settings > Partner Integrations in the Strava app. If you do not have a Readiness Score for the day, you may not receive your recap image.

Pairing AirPods for Heart Rate Tracking

Strava can read your heart rate in real time from Apple Health when you track it with your AirPods Pro 3. This feature is only available on iOS 18 or later.

Pair Your AirPods with Strava

To use your AirPods for heart rate tracking:

  • Turn on your AirPods Pro 3 and ensure they’re connected to your iPhone.

  • Open the Strava app and tap Record to start recording an activity.

  • Your heart rate will appear live on the recording screen. If your heart rate isn’t displaying during a recording, please check the following:

  • Open the Health app on your iPhone and navigate to Strava. Tap Allow All to grant both read and write permissions.

  • Verify device compatibility: Live heart rate tracking via AirPods requires iOS 18 or later and AirPods Pro 3.

  • Start recording: Heart rate data only displays during an active recording, not before you start.

Pairing Sensors with the Strava app

The Strava mobile app (version 169 or higher) currently supports Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) heart rate monitors. Learn more about analyzing your performance with heart rate data.

How to Pair a Sensor

Before getting started, be sure to enable Bluetooth on your mobile device. Once you’ve done so, please follow these instructions:

  • Select Record from the bottom navigation bar.
  • Expand the menu by sliding it up from the bottom of your screen, and select Add a Sensor. The app will automatically begin searching for available sensors.
  • Wake your Bluetooth heart rate monitor (refer to the recording device manufacturer’s manual if you are unable to wake your device) so it may be discovered in the list of recording devices.
  • Tap your sensor to connect it once it appears.
  • Select Done to return to the record screen. Your real-time heart rate will be displayed during your recording.

Troubleshooting Sensor Connection Issues

  • Try toggling Bluetooth off and back on again in your phone’s settings.
    • iPhone: Ensure your Bluetooth privacy setting is toggled ON by visiting the Settings app → Privacy & Security → Bluetooth, then confirm the Strava toggle is set to the enabled position.
  • Check that the battery in your heart rate monitor is charged.
  • Be careful that your heart rate monitor has not paired with another device that’s within range. Bluetooth only allows you to pair with one device.

FAQs

What devices are compatible?

As long as the device broadcasts as a heart rate monitor for Bluetooth connections, it should be discoverable when you open the heart rate screen. However, due to the vast number of Bluetooth heart rate monitor devices, we cannot guarantee the effectiveness of each device. Most popular Bluetooth heart rate monitors from brands like Polar, Bryton, Garmin, and Wahoo should be compatible.

Please be sure that you’ve enabled Bluetooth functionality on your mobile device and that you have disconnected your heart rate monitor from other services such as Garmin Connect or Wahoo Fitness. Usually, Bluetooth devices such as heart monitors can only be connected to a single service at a time.

Can I pair power or cadence meters?

Our plan is to first roll out heart rate monitors with BLE pairing to ensure it’s working as intended before we expand to power/cadence meters or other sensors. We don’t have a hard timeline but if our rollout of BLE pairing works as planned, you can expect power/cadence meter support to be recording devices that we would look at to support in the future. In the meantime, these sensors can be paired with the Wahoo Fitness app. When you connect your Wahoo Fitness and Strava apps, activities recorded with Wahoo Fitness that include other sensor data will automatically upload to Strava. More information about how to connect your accounts can be found here.

Can I pair an ANT+ device?

At this time, we don’t have any plans to adopt ANT+ into our mobile application due to its limited availability on mobile devices. While we cannot guarantee its effectiveness, you’re welcome to explore what is considered to be a bridge device on your own. Bridge devices will allow you to connect ANT+ sensors via Bluetooth to your Strava recording. We do not endorse just any one brand of bridge device as we aren’t actively supporting these types of connections, but you can find an example of one here: npe-inc.com

Partner Integrations

Partner integrations refer to activities in the feed associated with certain services of our partners. These integrations highlight unique stats or visuals, which may include an image from the partner and a default activity title.

How it Works

Partner integrations are viewable by both the uploading athlete and their followers. Activities recorded as part of a partner integration receive enhanced treatment if the athlete uploading the activity has the integration enabled.

Athlete Controls

As an uploader, you have the option to disable this enhanced treatment of your activities without affecting the way your activity data is synced with Strava. You can manage all partner integrations using the mobile app or on the Strava website under Settings > Partner Integrations. Please keep in mind:

  • You may only enable or disable this treatment on your own activities.
  • Opting out of the experience means you will not see any of the enhanced partner content on your own activities; however, your basic activity data will continue to sync and show in the feed.

FAQ

I don’t want to see this treatment in my feed. How do I turn it off?

The ability to disable enhanced treatment is controlled by the activity’s owner.

Where can I see a full list of Partner Integrations?

You can find a full list of integrations and learn more about connecting each app at strava.com.

Peloton and Strava

Peloton offers live and on-demand group fitness classes led by elite NYC instructors from the comfort and convenience of your home. Please follow the steps below to connect and share your Peloton activities with Strava.

For Peloton All-Access Members with a Peloton Bike, Bike+, Tread, or Row:

  • Sign in to your Peloton Account on either your Peloton Bike, Bike+, Tread, or Row.
  • Go to your Profile Settings and then tap on Connected Apps. You will then see an option to connect with Strava if you haven’t done so already.
  • Once Strava is connected, navigate to your dashboard and select Account, then Workout History.
  • Tap on the workout you would like to upload to Strava and then click Share. You will also have the option to share your workout with Strava right after you complete a Peloton class.

To enable auto-sync on your Bike, Bike+, Tread, or Row, follow the steps below:

  • Go to your account settings by tapping on your username in the top left corner of your home screen.
  • Tap the Social button, then select the option to auto-post your workouts to Strava. This feature can be turned on and off whenever you want.

For Peloton Members with an App One or App+ Membership:

  • Sign in to your Peloton Account on members.onepeloton.com.
  • Go to your Preferences and select the Settings tab. Scroll down to Connected Networks. If you haven’t already, you will see an option to connect to Strava.
  • Once you’ve connected Strava, navigate to your home screen, then select Profile and Workout History.
  • Tap the workout you want to upload to Strava, and then click Share.
When connecting to Strava via members.onepeloton.com, auto-post will be enabled by default. To change the setting:

  • Go to Preferences by clicking on the three bars at the top right of your screen.

  • Click on Settings and scroll down to Connected Networks.

  • Remove the checkmark beside “Automatically share my workout activity with Strava.” You can also control your Strava auto-post settings on your Bike, Bike+, Tread, or Row, or through members.onepeloton.com. Once enabled, your Peloton workouts will then sync automatically with Strava. Strava also offers you a way to report media on the app and website by clicking on the Report option. These settings cannot be changed on the Peloton mobile app, only on the website.

Polar and Strava

You can automatically upload your activities to Strava from Polar Flow. Connect your Polar Flow and Strava accounts through your settings on Polar Flow. For more information, please refer to Polar’s online instructions.

  • Once connected, new activities will be synced directly to Strava from Polar Flow Sync, the Polar Flow app, or Polar Beat.
  • Historical activities will not transfer over once you connect your account so you will need to use Polar’s export option and then upload the file manually to Strava.
  • You can link several Polar Flow accounts to one Strava account.
  • If you have a private Polar Flow account, your activities will upload to Strava as Private.

Troubleshooting Syncing

Be aware that activities that meet the criteria below will not sync to Strava. If none of these apply to your activity, the best option is to export the original from Polar Flow and upload it to Strava from our upload page.

  • Manually added activities.

  • Training sessions that have been synced with Polar group solutions or from third-party applications or services, for example, Polar Club or MyFitnessPal.

  • Training sessions that have been transferred to Polar Flow from polarpersonaltrainer.com or from Polar ProTrainer 5.

  • Training sessions that have been synced to Polar Flow before connecting Polar Flow to Strava. These training sessions can be transferred to Strava with Polar Flow’s export function.

Power and Cadence Data from Apple Health

Cycling activity data recorded on Apple’s native Workout app with a power meter and/or cadence sensor will now sync to Strava. Please follow the steps in this article, to connect your Apple Health to your Strava account.

Compatible Devices

Indoor and outdoor cycling activities recorded with the Apple Workout app will include power and cadence data if those sensors are connected to the watch. Power and cadence data are displayed on the activity detail page within the mobile app and web.

​

Ensure you’ve allowed Strava to read power and cadence data. To make sure Strava can access your power and cadence data, take the following steps:

  • From your iPhone, go to your settings and select: Health > Data Access & Devices > Strava > Toggle all available options on.
  • ​
  • Accept all health data permissions.
  • Accept the new permissions from Apple Health, even if you have previously connected with Health. Open Strava and tap on the Settings icon, then Manage Apps & Devices > Health > and tap ‘Connect with Health’. New activities will now display power and cadence if available in the file. Please be aware that only activities recorded with the Apple Watch Workout app recorded within the past 30 days are able to sync to Strava. Activities uploaded to the Health app from a third party will not sync to Strava.

FAQ

Why aren’t my cadence and power data displayed on Strava after I synced my cycling activity from the Apple Fitness app?

To see cycling power & cadence information from Healthkit on your Strava app, you’ll need iOS 17+, watchOS 10+, and Strava app version 403+. Please also ensure you’ve accepted the necessary data permissions by following the steps above, even if you’ve done so previously.

What about running power and cadence data from Health?

Strava only supports running power data from Healthkit. We do not support cadence information at this time. To view power data for your running activities on the activity details page in the mobile app, ensure you have granted the necessary data permissions. Power data will not be displayed on the web and it will not be factored into an athlete’s Fitness & Freshness or Power Curve.

Relative Effort on Suunto devices

Strava subscribers can see Live Relative Effort during activity recordings on their Suunto devices.

Compatible Devices

  • Suunto 5
  • Suunto 9

Enabling Live Relative Effort

You will need to enter the same maximum heart rate or custom heart rate zones in your Suunto watch as they appear in Strava in order to get the same score when viewing the activity on your Strava account.

  • To do this on your watch, navigate to Settings > Training > Intensity Zones > Default Zones.

  • Use your max heart rate and heart rate zones in your Strava profile settings.​ To enable live Relative Effort:

  • On your watch, go to Exercise.

  • Select the sport you want to record (i.e. running or cycling.)

  • When you are in the specific sport mode, open options.

  • Select Sports Apps.

  • Enable Strava.

  • Go back and start the exercise.

  • During exercise, use the middle button to switch screens until you see the Strava Relative Effort screen (as seen below).

  • ​

  • The Strava display now shows the real-time Relative Effort value and Duration.

  • You can review your Relative Effort score in the activity summary on the watch and then on Strava.com.

FAQ

Can free Strava athletes take advantage of Live Relative Effort?

You will see your Relative Effort on your device, but if you’re not a Strava subscriber, it will not appear in your activity details.

Can I get Live Relative Effort if I’m recording indoor or stationary activities?

Yes, indoor cycling and treadmill recordings do not need extra sensors.

ROUVY and Strava

If you record activities with ROUVY, you can automatically or manually upload your activities to Strava by connecting your accounts. Please be aware that you can only connect one ROUVY account to each Strava account.

  • Log in to your account on the ROUVY website.
  • In the top-right corner, click on your icon and choose Connected Apps and Devices from the drop-down menu.
  • You will be taken to a Connected Apps tab, where you can see your already Connected Apps and Available Apps to connect.
  • In the Available Apps list, find Strava and click Connect.
  • Confirm and log in to your Strava account to authorize the connection.

Automatic & Manual Activity Exports

You can toggle the slider next to the Strava logo to switch between automatic and manual activity exports. When toggled On, your syncing will be set to automatic, and when toggled Off, you will need to select the activities you wish to sync to Strava manually.

  • If you select auto, your activities will be automatically uploaded to Strava immediately after they’re created.
  • If you select manual, you’ll have to click the share option each time you would like to upload an activity.

Indoor & Outdoor Connection

ROUVY combines outdoor and indoor activities - you can import your ‘outdoor’ activities from Strava and collect points for them in ROUVY’s Career feature.

There are 3 conditions that need to be fulfilled to be eligible for earning Coins for your Outdoor rides.

  • You need to set up the Automatic connection with Strava.
  • Only activities recorded via the Strava app on your device are eligible - no 3rd party data providers are supported - e.g. uploading ride from your cycling computer.
  • The activity visibility must be set to “Everyone”. Please note that any activity that includes data using Rouvy’s ‘gamified’ settings, such as reduced gradients or boosts, will have segments automatically excluded. This is the intended functionality following Rouvy and our leaderboard system.

FAQs

Why are some of my virtual rides not counting towards leaderboards?

​Please note that any activity that includes data using Rouvy’s ‘gamified’ settings will have segments automatically excluded. This is the intended functionality following Rouvy and our leaderboard system. You can read more about what types of data will result in your virtual ride being tagged as gamified on Rouvy’s support page.

Samsung Galaxy Watch and Strava

If you have a Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 or Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and live in a territory where Strava is available, you’re eligible for a one-time 60-day Strava subscription trial. Before you redeem, make sure you’re signed in to the Strava app on your Galaxy Watch.

How to redeem your 60-day trial

  • Open the Strava app on your Android phone.
  • Tap Settings > Promotions.
  • Follow the prompts to redeem your 60-day free trial.

Things to know

  • This offer is available to free Strava accounts only.
  • You must have purchased a Galaxy Watch 9 or Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 to be eligible.
  • This is a limited-time offer, available until July 31, 2027.
  • The offer has no cash value.
  • The 60-day trial converts into an auto-renewing annual subscription at the end of the trial.
  • To activate the offer, open the Strava app on the watch and link it to the Strava mobile app.

FAQs

I’m already a Strava subscriber. Can I redeem this trial?

Not right away. You’ll need to cancel your current subscription and wait until it ends before you can redeem the 60-day trial. Your existing subscription must end before July 31, 2027, for you to be eligible.

After I sign up for the trial, how do I manage my subscription?

Your subscription renews automatically unless you cancel at least 24 hours before your renewal date. To manage it:

  • Open the Strava app and go to the You tab.
  • Tap the gear icon to open Settings.
  • Select Your Strava Subscription > Manage Your Subscription. You can also manage your subscription directly through Google Play.

Sending Extra Information from iOS to Support

Finding Crash Log Files

When the Strava app crashes or closes unexpectedly on your iPhone, you can help us understand the cause by sending us crash logs. These are data files created by the operating system in the event of a crash, and they are beneficial to our engineering team when they are working on fixing the issue.

Application Data

In some cases, the support team may request that you send the data stored in the Strava application for troubleshooting. This data includes your Strava activity and settings information used by the Strava app. You can use the Apple App Store to back up the data on your iOS device to your computer’s hard drive.

Plug the device into your computer, and open the Apple App Store. Make sure the “Encrypt iPhone backup” option is DISABLED on the Apple App Store Summary screen. The backup created should not be encrypted, and it should not have a padlock icon next to it.

Download the computer program for your computer’s operating system below and install it:

  • Mac: supercrazyawesome.com (you can find an introduction and an example walkthrough here:) iclarified.com)
  • Windows: iphonebackupextractor.com This program lets you explore the data in the backup file and extract the files associated with the Strava iOS app. Navigate into these folders: “iOS Files”, “Library”, “Strava”. The files that end in “.sqlite” or “.sqlitedb” are Strava application data files that you can send to Strava support.

Create a support ticket and attach the file(s) you found on your hard drive. Please describe the actions leading up to the issue, along with any other information about your device and environment. Or you could send an email to [email protected] with the files attached.

Sign in With Apple

If you created a Strava account using your Apple ID by going to the sign-up page and clicking “Sign Up with Apple”, then you used Apple’s Hide My Email feature. This feature assigns a separate proxy email address to your Strava account, which appears as: [email protected]. Emails sent to your proxy email address are forwarded by Apple to the email address associated with your Apple account.

Change Your Email from the Proxy Address

You can change your email address from the proxy email assigned by Apple, but you’ll need to first set a password for your Strava account. Go to strava.com and enter the proxy email address that Apple assigned to your Strava account. You should receive a link to reset your password within minutes. Once you have set a password for your Strava account, you will be able to update your email address. Please refer to our article’ How to Change Your Email Address’ for more information.

When changing the email address on your Strava account and encountering the error message, “This is not a valid email address,” it’s possible that you already have a Strava account associated with that new email address. Please log out of your current account and delete this duplicate account. Then, log back in and update your email information.

Enable the Sign in with Apple Login Option

If you want to use Apple to sign in to your existing Strava account, please follow the instructions below:

  • Ensure that your Strava account uses the same email address as your Apple ID account.
  • The next time you log in to Strava, click the “Sign In with Apple” login option.
  • When you’re asked which email to use, you must select “Share your email”. You cannot use the option to hide your email if you would like to link to an existing Strava account. Your Strava account will then be automatically linked to your Apple ID account.

If you cannot access your Strava account or do not have access to your old email, please contact our support team and provide as much information as possible to help verify your account.

Siri Integration

Requirements

You can use Siri to start, pause, or resume your activity if you’re running iOS 12 or later and Strava 81.0.0 or later. You can use Siri whether or not you are using headphones.

How to use Siri with the Strava App

Any phrase that includes “Strava” and one of the following words or a combination of words will perform the respective action. You cannot use Siri to stop or finish a recording.

  • Start Activity: Ask Siri to start a recording on Strava. The activity type will default to whichever type you recorded last.
  • Pause: Ask Siri to pause a recording that’s already in progress.
  • Resume: Ask Siri to resume an in-progress recording that’s been paused.

Enabling Siri Shortcuts

To use custom phrases, you can enable Siri Shortcuts. From the mobile app, open your settings from the icon in the upper right corner of the You tab. Select Siri & Shortcuts > Go to Settings > Siri & Search > Toggle Use with Ask Siri on.

Strava Snapchat Lens

A few situations can trigger another person’s Garmin data uploading to your Strava account. Strava and Tractive

Integrate your Tractive and Strava app to share your dog’s activities and track your fitness goals. Follow these steps to connect your Tractive and Strava App.

In the Tractive app for iOS and Android:

  • Open the Tractive app and tap the Account tab in the lower right corner.
  • Scroll down and select Connect Apps.
  • From the Connect Apps page, connect with Strava.
  • Tap on Continue and you will be prompted to Authorize the connection. A confirmation that you have successfully connected accounts should appear after authorization. You cannot connect your Strava account to multiple Tractive accounts or vice versa. If you would like to disconnect Strava from your Tractive App, follow the above steps, and in Connect Apps click Remove next to Strava.

Recording and Uploading Walks:

Once connected, any walk recorded on Tractive will automatically upload to your Strava account. A walk can only be saved in the Tractive app when it lasts a minimum of 1 minute and covers more than 0 meters.

To record a walk:

  • Go to the Map tab in the bottom left corner.

  • Select Walk and begin to record.

  • When you are finished, press End to stop the recording.

  • Your activity will automatically sync to your connected Strava account. When you use Tractive to track your walk, the app records how long your walk lasts by noting when you start and stop it with a button press. However, the app stops recording your location if you stop moving before you press the button to end your walk. This means the last location sent to Strava has a timestamp from before you press the button to stop. So, the time Strava shows for your walk might be shorter than the duration you see in the Tractive app. Please note that you cannot manually synchronize your walks to Strava, and if a walk is updated or deleted in the Tractive app, it will not be reflected on Strava.

Strava API and MCP FAQ

Does this mean that I lose access to my data?

No. It’s your data. Every user, including free users, is able to access their data through the free Strava app, the free Strava website, and download their data directly, for free.

Are you shutting off the API?

No. We are making changes to make it more secure, provide better support to developers, and stop the flood of poorly written AI-generated apps and data scraping that was impairing platform performance and reliability for everyone.

Why are you making these changes now?

Keeping the developer platform secure, reliable, and useful is continuous and ongoing work. How developers build has changed radically over time—most recently with the rapid adoption of AI, which has shifted both usage patterns and the platform’s risk profile. So we’re modernizing it again, with three priorities: stronger security, better support for the developers building real value for athletes, and strict protections against data scraping and high-volume, low-quality traffic that degrades performance and reliability for everyone.

Did you consult with any developers before you made these changes?

Yes, we consulted with many developers as we were planning these changes. They understand the problems we are solving and appreciate that this will increase the support that we can provide them. We have also heard the frustration from the massive number of developers who were stuck in the application queue and this solves that as well.

What is going to happen to my favorite integrated app/device?

In the vast, vast majority of cases, it will continue to work. There are 140 multi-user apps (0.06% of all apps) that will require changes to continue to integrate with Strava. We have reached out to all of them and will support them through the transition. Once that work is done, their apps will continue to work as well.

How many developers are going to be affected by these changes?

There are 140 multi-user apps (0.06% of all apps) that will require changes to continue to integrate with Strava. We have reached out to all of them and will support them through the transition. Once that work is done, their apps will continue to work as well.

Why is only Strava doing this?

Strava is by no means the only platform with a public API that deals with massive data scraping, and a flood of poor-quality zero-code apps causes review queue backlogs and platform performance problems. What is different in this approach is that we have found a way to continue to support access for hobbyist developers all the way up to major developers. We have also added new capabilities for individuals who want to interact directly with their data without coding.

Why is a subscription required?

It allows us to add subscription features to the MCP and the API. It also helps deter those who would seek to exploit the API.

What if I don’t like AI?

The MCP is an optional feature for subscribers, designed with security and ease-of-use in mind. No one is required to use it.

Why only Anthropic/Claude?

We are launching with Anthropic because we believe they will honor the terms not to use your data to train their models without your consent. We look forward to working with other AI platforms in the future that share our principles regarding the protection of user data.

Want to learn more? See our Press Release, Developer FAQ and MCP Connector

Strava Apple Watch App

Set up the Strava Apple Watch app

The Strava Apple Watch app supports watchOS 10.0 or later and iOS 17.0 or later. To get started, make sure you have the Strava app installed on your iPhone.

Install the app on your Apple Watch

Companion apps for iPhone are typically installed on your Apple Watch automatically. If the Strava app isn’t visible on your watch, install it manually:

  • Open the Apple Watch app on your iPhone and tap My Watch.

  • Find Strava in the list and tap Install.

  • Make sure you’re logged in to your Strava account on your iPhone.

  • Open the Strava app on your watch and follow the prompts to authorize permissions for Health and Motion & Fitness data.

  • On your iPhone, go to Settings > Apps > Health > Data Sources & Access > Strava. Toggle on Heart Rate and Workouts. If you don’t see all permission toggles:

  • On the Strava app, go to Settings > Manage Apps & Devices > Health and tap Connect with Health.

  • Then go to Settings > Apps > Health > Data Access and Devices > Strava and toggle on all necessary permissions.

Record an activity

You can record activities on Apple Watch Series 4 or later without carrying your iPhone. Note that the Apple Watch app functions independently of the iPhone app; your phone will not visibly respond while you record, even if it’s nearby.

  • Open the Strava app on your Apple Watch.
  • Choose your sport type to begin recording. A 3-second countdown will start; tap the screen to skip it.
  • During your recording, you can view your current time, heart rate, and sport-specific stats:
    • Outdoor run — Average pace of your current split or average overall pace. Tap the screen to toggle between the two.
    • Outdoor ride — Current speed.
  • To pause, swipe right and tap the pause button.
  • To finish, swipe left and tap Finish, then tap Save on the summary screen. Your activity will upload to Strava automatically when your phone is within range or your watch has a network connection. You’ll receive an in-app notification once the upload is complete. Note that there may be a short delay in syncing if your devices are not connected to Wi-Fi or are in low-power mode after extended use.

Record heart rate

To use the Apple Watch’s built-in heart rate monitor, Strava needs permission to read heart rate data from Apple Health. You do not need to enable Bluetooth or heart rate sensors in the Strava iPhone app.

  • Open the Strava app on your Apple Watch as if you’re about to record an activity. This will open a prompt on both your phone and watch.
  • On your iPhone, tap Open Strava and follow the prompts to allow Strava to access your Health data.
  • In Apple Health, scroll down to Allow Strava to Read Data and enable Heart Rate. Your heart rate will appear in the lower right corner of the Apple Watch record screen. Note that heart rate does not appear on the Strava iPhone app recording screen.

Follow a route

You can follow a saved Strava route on your Apple Watch while recording.

  • On the sport type selection screen, tap the Route icon and select the route you want to follow.
  • Once selected, your activity will start recording.
  • To view the map while recording, swipe up on your watch face. You can follow your live location and saved route on the map. Tap the watch face to unlock interactive mode for zooming and panning.
  • To return to the stats screen, tap the back icon or use the watch scroll button.

Off-route alerts

Strava can alert you when you go off-route during a recorded activity. Off-route alerts are available on the Strava Apple Watch app, mobile record (iOS and Android), and Live Activity (iOS).

When you record with a saved route loaded, Strava tracks your position relative to the route. If you move a meaningful distance away, an alert appears on your recording screen. The alert dismisses automatically once you return to the route. Minor GPS drift will not trigger it.

Off-route alerts are on by default. To toggle them:

  • Apple Watch — While recording, swipe left to the settings page and tap the Off-Route Alerts toggle.
  • Mobile — Open navigation settings from the recording screen. Turning alerts off won’t affect your ability to follow a route.

Requirements:

  • Apple Watch or iPhone/Android running the latest version of the Strava app
  • A saved route loaded before or during recording
  • Live Activity requires iOS 16.1 or later

Live elevation

You can view your current elevation and total elevation gain/loss on the record screen for these sport types:

  • Hiking
  • Trail Running
  • Cycling (MTB, e-MTB, Gravel, and Road)
  • Winter Sports (Alpine Ski, Snowboard, Backcountry, and Snowshoe)

Watch face complications

You can add Strava complications to your watch face from the Apple Watch app on your iPhone or directly on your watch. Available complication sizes: circular small (bottom left), utilitarian small (middle), or modular small (bottom right).

To add from your iPhone, open the Apple Watch app, select Modular, choose a location, and select Strava from the list.

To add from your watch, press and hold the watch face to enter the customization view, then swipe right to see which complications are available.

Troubleshooting

Heart rate isn’t recording

First, verify that Strava has permission to access your heart rate data. In the Apple Health app, go to Browse > Heart > Heart Rate > Data Sources & Access and make sure Heart Rate and Workouts are toggled on.

If permissions are already enabled:

  • Force-close the Strava app on both your Apple Watch and your iPhone.
  • Restart both devices.
  • After restarting, try recording a few different activity types to see if heart rate appears.
  • If the issue persists, try disabling Low Power Mode. In the Apple Watch app, go to Apps > Workout > Low Power Mode and toggle it off. Activity isn’t syncing from Apple Watch to Strava

There may be a brief delay when devices aren’t connected to Wi-Fi or are conserving battery after extended use. If the activity still hasn’t synced, try the following:

  • Check connectivity — Make sure your Apple Watch is within range of your iPhone or has a reliable internet connection.
  • Force quit and restart — On your Apple Watch, double-tap the digital crown, swipe the Strava app left, and tap the red X button. Restart the Strava app on both devices.
  • Trigger a manual sync — On your Apple Watch, go to Settings > Unsynced to view and manually sync any unsynced activities. Motion and Fitness option not appearing in Strava permissions

On your iPhone, go to Settings > Privacy > Motion & Fitness > Fitness Tracking and confirm the setting is enabled. If it’s already on, toggle it off and back on.

FAQs

Does the Apple Watch app support Strava Live Segments?

Yes. Live Segments are available on the Strava Apple Watch app.

Can I pair a Bluetooth LE chest strap with my Apple Watch?

Yes, compatible Bluetooth LE heart rate sensors can be paired with your Apple Watch.

Can I use Strava with other fitness trackers at the same time?

This is not recommended. Other workout apps that use the Apple Watch’s GPS may interfere with your Strava recording.

How is live elevation on Apple Watch calculated?

Live elevation is derived from your device’s motion sensor and requires motion permission in Strava. To grant access, go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Motion & Fitness. If motion access hasn’t been granted, live elevation will be calculated from GPS instead, which is less accurate.

My activity is missing data such as GPS, maps, or heart rate. What should I do?

Strava needs health data access to display activity data such as heart rate. Make sure you’ve allowed health data access to Strava by following the steps here. Then check that you’ve granted all necessary permissions by going to Settings > Apps > Health > Data Access & Devices > Strava and toggling on all permissions.

If an activity is missing specific data such as GPS, maps, or heart rate, that data cannot be added back in once the activity has been uploaded. If the missing data is due to permissions that weren’t previously granted, only activities uploaded after permissions are re-enabled will display that data — it cannot be applied retroactively.

Strava Beacon for Apple Watch

Beacon is available for subscribers on the Strava Apple Watch app on Series 2 and above. Beacon requires a cellular connection so if you have an Apple Watch with cellular connectivity, you can use Beacon without carrying your phone. If you have the Series 2, however, you will need to be carrying your phone to use Beacon with your Apple Watch app.

  • To set up Beacon on your Apple Watch, you must first follow the instructions above to choose your contacts from the Strava iPhone app.
  • Once you’ve done that, open the settings page in your Strava Apple Watch app and select Beacon.
  • Toggle ON the option to Use Beacon and Close the screen.
  • Beacon’s status on your settings page should now read Ready and a Beacon link will be sent to your safety contacts in a text message when you start recording provided that you are using an Apple Watch with a cellular connection or carrying a phone. Please be aware that the text will not be sent from your own phone number.
  • A shareable link will also become available on the Beacon settings page in the iPhone app once you’ve started your activity. You can copy this link and share it through any means you wish (email, WhatsApp, etc.)

FAQs

Why aren’t my Beacon texts being sent?

Please check that you have entered their full number including the country and area code starting with the + symbol. Please note that the + symbol is required for Beacon texts to be sent automatically from 3rd party devices.

Strava Beacon for Garmin Android

Strava subscribers can use Strava Beacon on their Garmin to share their real-time location with their family and friends.

Requirements

  • Strava mobile app
  • Strava subscription
  • Garmin Connect mobile app
  • Strava Beacon compatible Garmin device

Setting up Beacon in the Strava app

  • Open the Strava app, go to the Record screen, and swipe the menu up.
  • Tap Share Live Location and toggle Beacon For Mobile on.
  • Toggle on Garmin under Beacon For Devices and follow the prompts to turn on the Autostart feature in the Garmin Connect app.

Setting up Garmin Connect

  • If you have an Auto Start capable device, the option will appear, and you only need to enable it once.

Starting an activity

  • Pair your Garmin device with the Connect app via Bluetooth.
  • If you have Auto Start enabled, start your recording on your device and a Beacon link will be automatically sent to your Safety Contacts.
  • If you have Auto Start disabled, go to ‘LiveTrack’ in the side navigation menu and press the ‘Start LiveTrack’ button at the bottom of the screen, then start your recording on your device. You can start the recording first, then enable LiveTrack - but you will need to start both manually. Once you’ve started your recording, you will see a Beacon notification in the notification dropdown (A).

Tap the notification to return to the settings page to send additional Beacon links (B).

FAQs

Do I still need to carry my phone?

Yes, even though your Garmin is the device that is recording the GPS of your activity, you still will need your phone to transmit your location data to your safety contact.

Does my phone need a cellular signal for Beacon to work?

Yes, in order to send your location, your phone will need cellular service. If you lose service at any time during your activity, your location will be updated the next time you are back in service.

Are the text messages being sent from my phone number?

No, when using Beacon on Garmin, the text messages will be sent to your safety contact from a 3rd party, so the phone number of the text message will be different.

Why aren’t my Beacon texts being sent?
  • Please first check that your device and Garmin Connect mobile app are up to date.
  • Please check that you have entered their full number, including the country and area code, starting with the + symbol. Please note that the + symbol is required for Beacon texts to be sent automatically from 3rd party devices.
  • There are a few settings that can cause problems with Beacon, and some of them are unique to the make/model of Android, so please check the following:
    • Find and disable your phone’s battery saver settings. These are typically located in Settings > Battery > Hamburger (top right 3 dots) > Battery Saver (screenshot attached).
    • If your phone has a battery management mode, please turn it to “off” instead of “medium” or “high”.
For more information and use of Beacon’s other features, please visit the Strava Beacon page.

Strava Live Activities on iOS

Strava Live Activities let you view real-time stats from your recording directly on your iPhone Lock Screen or Dynamic Island, on supported devices. This makes it easier to check your progress without unlocking your phone.

How Live Activities work

When you start recording in the Strava app, a Live Activity automatically appears on your Lock Screen. If your device supports it, it will also appear in the Dynamic Island.

Live Activities display elapsed time, distance, and pace. You can tap the Live Activity to return to the Strava app and view more details or stop your recording. The Live Activity will end once you finish and save your activity.

The Live Activities feature requires an iPhone running iOS 16.1 or later. Dynamic Island is supported on iPhone 14 Pro, 14 Pro Max, and iPhone 15 series or newer.

How to enable Live Activities

Strava uses Live Activities automatically, but you’ll need to allow them in your iPhone settings:

  • Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  • Go to Face ID & Passcode and make sure Live Activities are allowed when the phone is locked.
  • Go to Settings > Strava > Live Activities, then turn on Allow Live Activities and More Frequent Updates (optional — this updates stats more often but may use more battery) Once these settings are enabled, Strava will automatically show Live Activities when you record.

How to turn off Live Activities

If you don’t want to see Live Activities while recording:

  • Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  • Go to Strava > Live Activities.
  • Toggle Allow Live Activities off. You’ll still be able to record normally in the Strava app.

FAQs

Will Live Activities drain my battery?

Live Activities use minimal battery, especially with the More Frequent Updates setting turned off. You can disable this option if you’re concerned about battery usage.

Can I customize which stats appear in the Live Activity?

Not at this time. Strava automatically shows elapsed time, distance, and pace.

Do Live Activities work with all activity types?

Live Activities appear for any activity type that supports in-app recording on iOS.

Strava Reward Integration with Adidas

Strava and adidas have partnered to reward athletes for their activities on Strava. Once connected, eligible GPS-tracked activities will automatically earn adiClub points, which can be redeemed for rewards through adiClub. This integration is currently available to athletes in the US and Canada.

How it works

Once your Strava and adiClub accounts are connected, eligible GPS-tracked runs, walks, hikes, and rides logged on Strava will automatically count toward adiClub points. Manual activities are not eligible. You can earn up to 80 adiClub points per day.

Point rates by region:

  • US — 3 points per mile for running, walking, and hiking; 2 points per mile for cycling.
  • Canada — 2 points per kilometer for running, walking, and hiking; 1 point per kilometer for cycling.

Connect your Strava and adidas accounts

  • Visit the adidas Club on Strava from your mobile device.
  • Tap the Connect account button on the Earn rewards with adidas card.
  • Create or sign in to your adiClub account. Your adiClub account must be based in the US or Canada to qualify.
  • Accept the terms and conditions, then review and authorize the data permission requests. You may be prompted to sign in to your Strava account.
  • Once connected, you’ll be redirected back to the adidas Club on Strava. A loyalty button will appear on the club page to help you access and view rewards on adiClub.

Disconnect your Strava and adidas accounts

You can disconnect your accounts at any time. Upon disconnection, you will no longer earn points for activities on Strava.

Option 1 — From the adidas Club page on the Strava app:

  • Tap Overview on the adidas Club page.

  • Tap Manage loyalty account.

  • Tap Manage access next to the partner. You’ll be redirected to your adiClub account settings, where you can revoke your Strava connection. Option 2 — From Strava app settings:

  • Go to Settings > Manage apps and devices > Link a rewards partner.

  • Under Connected, tap Manage access next to the partner name. You’ll be redirected to your adiClub account settings, where you can revoke your Strava connection. Option 3 — From the adiClub website:

  • Visit your profile settings on adiClub.

  • Under Account overview, click Connected accounts.

  • Click Disconnect account under Strava.

Redeem your adiClub points

Points can be redeemed through adidas for gear, apparel, experiences, and a Strava subscription. To redeem, visit your adiClub account in a web browser, go to your profile, and click Rewards to see available offers.

If points aren’t showing up

Only eligible GPS-tracked runs, walks, hikes, and rides logged on Strava will earn adiClub points. Make sure your activity is GPS-tracked and that your accounts are connected. For questions about point tracking and redemption, contact the adidas customer service team at 1-800-982-9337.

Supported Android Devices and Android Operating Systems

Android OS supported versions

Strava version 466 and later requires Android 8.0 or higher. Custom or open source Android builds, including CyanogenMod, GrapheneOS, and LineageOS, are not supported. Strava relies on Google Play services to function, so devices running de Googled or custom operating systems that do not include Google Play services will not be able to log in or use the app.

If your device can’t run Android 8

The Strava app will no longer work on devices running Android 7 or earlier. If your device is no longer supported, you can still access Strava at strava.com in any browser, or log in to your account on a compatible device.

For more information, see App Version Requirements Update.

Known device issues

Some Android devices have known GPS or system issues that can affect Strava’s recording. See our article, How to Fix Recording Issues on Huawei Phones, for more info. The following phones are not supported by the Strava mobile app:

  • Wiko Rainbow

  • Samsung Galaxy Ace 3

  • Samsung Galaxy Express 2 The following phones are known to experience issues where the OS cuts off the Strava app during recording:

  • Huawei Nova and Nova+

  • Huawei P8 and P8 Lite

  • Huawei G7 and G7 Plus

  • Huawei Mate 7, Mate S, Mate 8, and Mate 9

  • Huawei Honor 4C, Honor 6, Honor 6 Plus, and Honor 7

  • Huawei P9, P9 Plus, and P9 Lite

Xiaomi, Redmi, or POCO login issues

Some Xiaomi, Redmi, and POCO phones can’t log into Strava or open the app without a system update. This affects a subset of devices running outdated software. Xiaomi released a fix for this issue starting with HyperOS 3.

How to fix it

  • Update your phone’s software. Go to Settings > About phone > System update and install any available update.
  • Update Google Play services. After updating your phone’s software, follow these steps (link: mi.com) to update Play Services.
  • Restart your phone. If you still see an error after updating, restart your device. This resolves a known issue in which a background service must be reset before the fix takes effect. If you’ve completed all three steps and still can’t log in, contact Strava Support.

Note that “Xiaomi, Redmi, or POCO login issues” is meant as an H3 and “How to fix it” as an H4, and Settings, About phone, and System update are meant to be bolded; none of that formatting carries over in plain text, so you’ll want to reapply it once this is in Intercom.
